title: Chemical Kinetics
tagline: Rate laws, mechanisms, collision and transition-state theory, chain reactions, catalysis, surfaces, photochemistry and dynamics
summary: Kinetics asks how fast reactions go and by what path. This course turns rate measurements into rate laws and mechanisms, explains rates with collision theory and transition-state theory, and treats chain reactions, catalysis and oscillations, reactions at surfaces, photochemical kinetics and the dynamics of single reactive encounters.

chapters.title: Rate laws and their measurement
chapters.summary: Experimental methods for following reactions, initial rates and the isolation method, and integrated rate laws of zero, first and second order.

chapters.title: Reaction mechanisms
chapters.summary: Elementary steps and molecularity, consecutive and competing reactions, the steady-state approximation, pre-equilibria and rate-determining steps.

chapters.title: Collision theory
chapters.summary: Molecular collisions, the Maxwell–Boltzmann distribution of speeds, steric factors and the origin of the Arrhenius equation.

chapters.title: Transition-state theory
chapters.summary: The activated complex, the Eyring equation, enthalpies and entropies of activation, and kinetic isotope effects.

chapters.title: Chain reactions
chapters.summary: Radical chain mechanisms, the hydrogen–bromine reaction, chain branching and explosion limits.

chapters.title: Catalysis, autocatalysis and oscillating reactions
chapters.summary: Acid–base and homogeneous catalysis, catalytic cycles, autocatalysis, and oscillating reactions such as the Belousov–Zhabotinsky reaction.

chapters.title: Adsorption and reactions at surfaces
chapters.summary: Physisorption and chemisorption, the Langmuir and BET isotherms, and the Langmuir–Hinshelwood and Eley–Rideal mechanisms.

chapters.title: Photochemical kinetics
chapters.summary: Absorption and quantum yields, the rates of fluorescence, phosphorescence and energy transfer, and quenching and the Stern–Volmer equation.

chapters.title: Molecular reaction dynamics
chapters.summary: Potential energy surfaces, trajectories and molecular beams, and diffusion-controlled reactions in solution.
